html:
The Adnyamathanha, whose name means "hills people" or "rock people", are an Aboriginal Australian people of the northern Flinders Ranges in South Australia. Their language belongs to the Yura group.

Their country includes the great natural basin of Ikara, called Wilpena Pound in English, which is central to their Dreaming stories. Their neighbours were the Kuyani to the west, the Malyangapa to the east, the Pirlatapa to the north and the Nukunu to the south.

Sheep runs took the ranges in the 1850s and copper mines opened in the 1860s. In 1931 a mission was set up at Nepabunna, which remains an Adnyamathanha community.
